review_notes: I read the whole file and checked every @[simp] lemma. I also grepped the repository for uses of the duplicated lemma names. The only concrete simp-interface problem I found is the pair of identical @[simp] lemmas `twoJet_quotient_op_smul_mk` and `twoJet_op_smul_mk`. The other simp lemmas have distinct left-hand sides. `source_op_smul_mk` is stated for the source Rees module. `quotientOrderReesTwoJetCAct_mk` and `quotientOrderReesTwoJetAction_quotient` are directed normalisations. I did not recommend making `quotientOrderReesTwoJetCAct_apply` a simp lemma, because it would compete with `quotientOrderReesTwoJetCAct_mk`. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour that I observed.

findings.excerpt:
theorem twoJet_op_smul_mk
    (I : RightIdeal (PresentedWeyl k n))
    (r : OrderReesRing (n := n) k)
    (x : QuotientOrderReesModule k I) :
    MulOpposite.op (orderReesTwoJetQuotient (n := n) k r) •
findings.problem: Two @[simp] lemmas have identical hypotheses, left-hand sides and right-hand sides, and both are proved by `rfl`. Both are registered as simp rules for the same pattern `op (orderReesTwoJetQuotient r) • Submodule.Quotient.mk x`. That makes the simp set redundant, and there are two competing names for one rewrite. Only `twoJet_op_smul_mk` is used (lines 515 and 749). `twoJet_quotient_op_smul_mk` is not used anywhere in the repository.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `twoJet_quotient_op_smul_mk`, lines 474–482. Keep one @[simp] lemma, preferably under a name that says what it does, such as `twoJet_op_quotient_smul_mk`, and update the two `rw` uses.
findings.benefit: The simp set has a single canonical rule for pushing the two-jet scalar action through `Submodule.Quotient.mk`. Readers are no longer left guessing which of two identical lemmas is intended.
